defects.mechanism: find_ never descends below a non-leaf node: the C recurses into get_quadrant_(node, &test); the translation calls get_quadrant_(None, Some(&test)) (get_quadrant_ takes Option<&mut QuadtreeNode> and find_ holds only a shared reference), which always returns None. So quadtree_search returns None for every point once the root has split (two or more points stored), where the C returns the stored point.

confirmed_by_repair.repair: replace get_quadrant_(None, ..) in find_ by the same nw/ne/sw/se lookup on node_ref (run.py repair_patch)

check_exercises_defect.evidence: PtrTrans's unit tests are not shipped.

not_in_totals.why_not_counted: Not a wrong value, state or output: every return value, length and tree state agrees. The divergence is a user callback that the C invokes and the translation never does. It is the key-deallocation hook: PtrTrans's 'Free Judge' step removes memory-deallocation calls from the C before translating (quadtree_runLog.txt:24638 '// Removed: reset_node_(tree, root); // NOTE: Memory Deallocation Operation, NEED TO REMOVE'), and its metric excludes deallocation functions (paper Sec. 4.1.3). On every insert where the C calls key_free on a non-NULL key, the translation drops exactly that key (Rust Drop) during the same insert (per_insert_check). Listed for the author to decide; not in the totals.
not_in_totals.mechanism: The translation keeps the public field Quadtree.key_free as Option<&dyn FnMut(&dyn Any)> but never calls it (a FnMut cannot be called through a shared reference); on a duplicate insert the C calls tree->key_free(old_key) via reset_node_ (quadtree.c:103-107, node.c:28-32), the Rust overwrites root.key (quadtree.rs:107-113).

per_insert_check.note_on_rejected_inserts: when quadtree_insert rejects a point (returns 0, nothing stored) the C leaves the key with the caller and calls no key_free; the translation takes the key by value (Option<Box<dyn Any>>) and drops it. No C-visible channel shows this; it is the Rust ownership signature, not a key_free call.

cases.note: 'divergent' = UB-clean, precondition-respecting cases that differ: search (the find_ defect, counted) and key_free (listed in not_in_totals, not counted)

ub_excluded.note: Null-member-access cases: quadtree_search in the C dereferences NULL when the query path ends at an empty quadrant or outside every quadrant (find_ -> get_quadrant_ -> node_contains_ on a NULL child: empty tree, absent, outside, split-line and NaN queries); UBSan 'member access within null pointer' under clang and gcc. Stack-overflow cases: bounds +/-1e308 (width overflows to inf) make split_node_ produce a child equal to its parent, so insert_ recurses without end (ASan stack-overflow; at -O3 the tail call becomes a loop that allocates until malloc fails; the Rust overflows its stack). Every one of these cases is a C crash with sanitizer evidence; none is counted.

precondition_only.rule: quadtree_new / quadtree_node_with_bounds name their parameters (minx, miny, maxx, maxy): an input with min > max violates the names. No other precondition is stated (header, README, comments).
precondition_only.note: every divergence on such inputs (bounds 10,10,1,1) is one of the two mechanisms that also diverge on valid inputs; these cases are left out of the exposure counts, and no mechanism diverges only on them.

c_implementation_dependent.note: the clang build's output differs from the gcc -O3 reference with no sanitizer report, and only within the float tolerance (signed zero from fmin/fmax on +/-0 inputs, which C leaves unspecified); all of these cases agree with the Rust, so nothing is affected. An ad-hoc re-run (not saved) found the differing tokens are only +0/-0 and the Rust equals the clang build bit for bit on all of them.
